name: Capacitive Nerve Induction Lance CNIL-1 'Threadneedle'
description:
The Capacitive Nerve Induction Lance is a precision energy weapon designed around a principle of extreme selectivity: rather than disrupting broad bioelectric function, it delivers a tightly focused capacitive discharge along a single projected electromagnetic filament — colloquially called 'the thread' — that is thin enough to target individual nerve trunks at range. The filament is maintained by a phased-array antenna system in the weapon's emitter head that continuously adjusts to compensate for atmospheric interference. At point of contact, the discharge induces a violent, involuntary nerve firing in the targeted structure — a single motor nerve produces a full-force muscle contraction; a sensory nerve produces an overwhelming pain signal; autonomic nerves produce effects that vary unpredictably and dangerously.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the CNIL-1 under their 'Precision Compliance' research program, initially as a surgical adjunct for nerve stimulation procedures in patients with certain degenerative conditions. The military application was recognized almost immediately by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS, which licensed the core technology and collaborated on the combat-ready version. The result is a weapon that demands exceptional operator training — hitting a specific nerve trunk at range requires detailed anatomical knowledge and a steady hand — but rewards that training with effects that no other platform can replicate. A shot to the brachial plexus drops a weapon instantly. A shot to the vagus nerve can stop a heart.

The weapon's cultural cachet is built on exclusivity and expertise. Threadneedle operators are known in professional circles as 'knitters' — a term that acknowledges both the weapon's filament mechanism and the surgical precision of skilled use. In assassination circles, a confirmed vagus-nerve kill is considered a mark of extraordinary craft, discussed with the kind of hushed respect usually reserved for master artisans. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS is aware of this reputation and has done nothing to discourage it.
manufacturer: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS (core technology) / ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (combat application)
specifications:
effective range: 25m (precision targeting), 40m (area effect, degraded)
filament diameter: ~2mm at 25m
discharge voltage: 2,200V capacitive burst (adjustable 800V–3,500V)
targeting system: Phased-array antenna with atmospheric compensation algorithm
power source: HELIX Microcapacitor Array HMC-2 (30 precision shots per array)
weight: 1.4 kg
length: 41 cm
charge cycle: 0.8 seconds between shots
operator requirement: Advanced anatomical training recommended
tactical_use: Threadneedle operators typically work from elevated positions or concealment, selecting specific nerve targets to achieve precise tactical outcomes — disarming without killing, inducing cardiac events that appear natural, or causing targeted incapacitation without leaving conventional wound evidence. In close-protection operations, skilled operators can neutralize a target in a crowd without adjacent individuals being aware anything has occurred. The weapon's limited shot count and charge cycle make it unsuitable for sustained firefights; it is a precision instrument, not a suppression tool.
cultural_context: The Threadneedle exists at the intersection of craft and violence in a way that fascinates Meridian 88's professional underground. Collectors of rare weapons prize confirmed CNIL-1 units regardless of operational condition. Assassination brokers charge significant premiums for confirmed 'knitter' kills. The weapon has also developed an unlikely following among certain HELIX BIOSYSTEMS researchers who see the combat application as a perversion of their surgical tool — several have become vocal critics of the ARCTURUS licensing arrangement, with mixed results for their continued employment.
story_hooks: A senior executive died of apparent cardiac arrest during a public event. The coroner found nothing. A fixer with forensic contacts suspects vagus nerve induction but needs proof — and proof requires finding the operator.

A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS researcher has gone public about the ARCTURUS licensing deal, claiming the combat application violates the original research ethics agreement. She's received three formal warnings. Now she's missing.

A Threadneedle has appeared on the black market with its phased-array antenna modified to project multiple simultaneous filaments — an area-effect version. HELIX considers this technically impossible. Someone proved them wrong.
A known 'knitter' has retired and is teaching. Word is spreading through professional circles about where the classes are held. Multiple parties want that list of students.
ammunition_type: Helix Biosystems Compact Power Cell HB-3
